title: Anthropic at $900B: funding, Mythos, and the agentic wave — May 26
summary: Anthropic is closing a funding round that could value it at over $900 billion — the largest AI valuation on record — as its quarterly revenue doubles and its Mythos model uncovers more than 10,000 cybersecurity vulnerabilities. TD Bank has deployed an agentic AI model to automate mortgage and home equity applications, the most concrete financial-services deployment this week. Practitioners should watch DeepSeek's permanent 75 percent price cut on its flagship model, which now tops global cost-efficiency rankings, and the new auth.md open protocol from WorkOS, which solves agent authentication without human sign-up flows.

script:
Your Daily AI Press Review — May 26, 2026: Agentic surge.

Anthropic is closing a round that could value it at over $900 billion — the largest AI valuation on record — as quarterly revenue doubles. DeepSeek makes a 75 percent price cut permanent, topping global cost-efficiency rankings and putting pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic pricing. Goldman Sachs projects a 24-fold surge in global token consumption by 2030 as agentic AI reshapes tech cash flows. Off the radar, Alipay has quietly processed 300 million AI-agent payments and launched the world's first large-scale AI-native payment infrastructure.

Anthropic is set to close a funding round that could raise over $30 billion and push its valuation above $900 billion, according to Bloomberg. The round could close this week, though commitments are still being finalized. The timing coincides with a doubling of quarterly revenue, which confirms that enterprise demand for Claude is accelerating faster than almost any prior AI product cycle. At that valuation, Anthropic would surpass most publicly listed financial institutions in market capitalization, making it the most valuable private AI company in history.

DeepSeek has made permanent a 75 percent promotional price cut on its V4 Pro flagship model, originally introduced one month after the model's launch. The Hangzhou-based startup is now ranked by Artificial Analysis as the world's top model on an intelligence-per-dollar basis, outperforming both OpenAI and Anthropic on cost efficiency. The permanent cut compresses the economics of LLM deployment for any enterprise running high-volume inference workloads, and it arrives as DeepSeek's V4 generation — comprising V4 Pro and a lighter variant — gains traction across Asian markets.

Goldman Sachs published research projecting that agentic AI will drive a 24-fold increase in global token consumption by 2030, reaching 120 quadrillion tokens processed annually. The bank argues this shift will materially increase free cash flow at major technology companies as inference revenue scales faster than infrastructure costs. The report frames autonomous AI agents — systems that plan, act, and iterate without human prompting — as the primary driver of that demand curve, and positions NVIDIA as the principal hardware beneficiary of the cycle.

Google used I/O 2026 to launch a sweeping set of agentic products, including new Gemini models, an autonomous assistant called Gemini Spark, upgraded AI search, AI glasses, and a $100-per-month Ultra plan targeting developers and power users. The company also released Google Antigravity 2.0, a full platform pivot from AI-assisted coding to multi-agent orchestration as the core development model. Separately, Google open-sourced an Agent Executor tool designed to support AI agents running in production environments, giving enterprise teams a reference implementation for agent lifecycle management.

Anthropic's Mythos Preview model has identified more than 10,000 cybersecurity vulnerabilities under Project Glasswing, the company's initiative to use AI to counter AI-powered cyberattacks. The disclosure positions Mythos as an offensive security tool capable of operating at a scale no human red team could match. Separately, Anthropic is expected to continue supplying Claude models to the NSA despite being flagged as a supply chain risk by the Pentagon — a deal that reportedly avoids the controversial 'any lawful use' clause that derailed earlier negotiations.

Catena Labs, led by Circle co-founder Sean Neville, raised $30 million and received acceptance from the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for a national trust bank charter application. The company is building regulated financial infrastructure specifically designed for AI agents — systems that can hold, move, and settle funds autonomously. It's the first agentic-native bank charter application in the US, and it arrives as agentic commerce infrastructure becomes a distinct investment category.

Xiaomi's latest open-source model, MiMo-V2.5-Pro, has been ranked by Artificial Analysis as the world's top open-source model for agentic capabilities. The Beijing-based company is embedding the model across its smartphone and electric vehicle product lines, treating AI as the connective layer across its hardware empire. Xiaomi's strategy — open-sourcing frontier agentic models while monetizing through hardware — mirrors Meta's approach and puts direct pressure on closed-model providers competing for developer mindshare in Asia.

ByteDance's AI-generated short films made headlines at the 79th Cannes Film Festival, with two works produced using the company's Seedance 2.0 model selected from more than 1,000 submissions across 120 countries for the Marché du Film showcase. The films — The Golden Tomb Seeker and Series Tower — were created by Chinese platform Chushou AI. A third ByteDance-linked production, Hell Grave, drew separate industry attention. The Cannes selection marks the first time AI-generated content has reached the festival's official business market at this scale.

Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya set a $350 price target on NVIDIA, citing what he calls an unprecedented chip cycle driven by agentic AI demand. Memory costs now represent about 63 percent of total AI chip costs, according to analysis from Gigazine, pushing the industry into an era where memory is more expensive than the GPU itself. Samsung chip workers are set to receive an average bonus of about $340,000 as the AI hardware boom flows through to labor compensation in South Korea's semiconductor sector.

On deployments. TD Bank has launched an agentic AI model that automates mortgage and home equity line of credit applications end-to-end. The system handles document intake, verification steps, and application routing without human intervention at each stage. TD is Canada's second-largest bank by assets, and the deployment targets one of the most document-intensive and latency-sensitive processes in retail banking. No public figure has been released for processing time reduction, but the bank framed the launch as a structural change to its origination workflow rather than a pilot.

Dick's Sporting Goods launched Coach by Dick's, a conversational AI tool embedded across its retail and digital channels. The system is designed to guide athletes through sport selection, performance gear recommendations, and training advice in a single dialogue session. Dick's operates more than 850 stores across the US, giving the deployment significant reach at the point of sale. The tool represents a shift from search-based product discovery to intent-driven conversation as the primary retail interface for sports equipment.

Alipay announced that its AI payment infrastructure has processed 300 million AI-agent transactions and now supports 95 percent of common agentic frameworks. The company simultaneously launched the world's first Token Pay service and an AI wallet product, completing what it calls a full-stack AI-native payment system. The scale — 300 million completed transactions — makes Alipay's agentic payment layer the largest commercially deployed infrastructure of its kind globally, ahead of any Western equivalent.

Meituan, China's dominant on-demand delivery platform, published a Skill API that allows any AI assistant to trigger a delivery order in a single conversational turn. The system handles scene recognition, address matching, price estimation, and order submission automatically, compressing what was previously a multi-step in-app flow. Partners already integrated include OpenClaw, Cursor, WeChat, and Feishu. The deployment is the clearest example yet of a major consumer platform restructuring its interface layer for AI-agent access rather than human navigation.

A Chinese AI marketing firm, Jisi Technology, reported over 60 billion RMB in cumulative GMV generated through AI-powered digital-human live commerce since 2022, serving brands including LVMH, L'Oréal, Procter and Gamble, Nestlé, and Diageo. The company operates across JD.com, Taobao, and Shopee, and launched the first official digital-human livestream on Shopee Taiwan in November 2024 with L'Oréal. Jisi describes its model as moving from 'using AI' to 'managing AI,' with a claimed tenfold efficiency gain in marketing content production.

Mercer found that a majority of asset managers now use AI in their investment process, according to a survey published this week by Fund Selector Asia. The finding marks a threshold crossing — AI has moved from experimental to standard practice in institutional investment workflows. The survey did not specify which tasks AI handles most frequently, but prior Mercer research has pointed to data aggregation, portfolio screening, and risk flagging as the primary use cases at firms that have crossed the adoption threshold.

KPMG launched an AI trust hub in Singapore to help enterprises assess, govern, and deploy AI systems at scale. The hub offers structured frameworks for model auditing, bias testing, and compliance documentation. Singapore's government agencies EnterpriseSG and IMDA simultaneously released a refreshed Retail Industry Digital Plan that provides SME retailers with a step-by-step AI adoption roadmap. The two launches together signal that Singapore is positioning itself as the governance infrastructure hub for AI deployment across Southeast Asia.

On tools. WorkOS released auth.md, an open agent registration protocol built on OAuth standards. The spec defines a Markdown file that any web application can publish at its domain, telling AI agents which registration flows are supported, which permission scopes to request, and how to obtain credentials tied to a real user — without requiring a human to complete a sign-up form. MCP has crossed 97 million monthly SDK downloads, and auth.md directly addresses the authentication gap that has blocked agents from accessing credentialed enterprise systems at scale.

Researchers from the University of Maryland, Google, and Meta used AutoTTS — a coding agent built on Claude — to autonomously discover a new compute-scaling algorithm for AI reasoning. The algorithm cuts compute by about 70 percent compared to standard self-consistency methods while matching their accuracy. The entire search cost $40 and took 160 minutes. The result is directly actionable: teams running inference-heavy reasoning pipelines can now treat algorithm discovery itself as an automated task rather than a research project.

Microsoft Copilot has been shown to fabricate country-level differences in data analysis when users leave model selection on default. Mathematician Adam Kucharski fed the tool identical datasets with different country labels and received detailed but invented stereotypes. Thinking models catch the error — but only when users know to select them manually. The practical implication: any analyst using Copilot, Gemini, or similar tools for comparative data work should explicitly select a reasoning-capable model rather than accepting the default.

Researchers at Peking University introduced CiteVQA, the first benchmark designed to test attribution hallucination — the failure mode where AI models cite text passages that don't actually support their answers. Leading models including GPT and Gemini routinely exhibit this behavior even when the answer itself is correct. For legal, compliance, and medical teams using AI for document analysis, CiteVQA provides the first systematic tool to measure citation reliability, which is distinct from answer accuracy and has been largely unmeasured until now.

ByteDance Seed published research showing that a 7-billion-parameter model trained by answering questions — rather than transcribing text — can outperform much larger models on long, image-heavy documents, even when those documents are four times longer than anything in its training set. The technique, called question-driven training, is immediately applicable to enterprise document intelligence pipelines where teams are choosing between large expensive models and smaller deployable ones for contract review, financial filings, and regulatory documents.

One signal to watch. AI adoption in the US crossed a threshold between December 2025 and January 2026, with daily active use reaching record speed according to a PYMNTS study. Separately, a University College London survey found that 96 percent of Chinese respondents use AI at work every week, and fewer than 10 percent worry about job displacement — a strikingly different sentiment profile from Western markets. The divergence in adoption intensity and anxiety levels between China and the US suggests that enterprise AI rollout velocity will differ significantly across geographies, with implications for competitive benchmarking.

Memory costs now represent about 63 percent of total AI chip costs, according to analysis cited by Gigazine, and SK Hynix has unveiled self-cooling iHBM chips specifically designed to address AI overheating at scale. Separately, AMD has committed $10 billion to Taiwan manufacturing, and Japan's Sakura Internet is planning to increase its capital expenditure to nearly seven times its original 2026 forecast — up to 30 billion yen — to meet domestic AI demand. These three data points together signal that the AI infrastructure bottleneck is shifting from GPU compute to memory bandwidth and thermal management, with Asian suppliers positioned as the primary beneficiaries.

George Hotz, after six months of testing AI coding agents, publicly concluded they will become one of the industry's most costly mistakes — producing fast prototypes but generating bugs that compound over time and become harder to isolate. His position sits at one extreme of a deeply split practitioner community. At the same time, Google's Antigravity 2.0 platform and AutoTTS's $40 algorithm discovery both demonstrate measurable gains from agentic coding in constrained, well-defined tasks. The gap between open-ended software development and bounded agentic tasks is emerging as the critical variable in evaluating coding agent ROI.

Off the radar. Japan's Sakura Internet, a domestic cloud and data center provider, is planning to raise its fiscal 2026 capital expenditure to as much as 300 billion yen — nearly seven times the 44 billion yen it announced in April — to meet surging domestic AI demand. CEO Kunihiro Tanaka confirmed the company intends to procure new GPUs within the current fiscal year ending March 2027. This is not a hyperscaler story. Sakura Internet is a mid-tier national provider, and its capex explosion reflects a second wave of AI infrastructure investment hitting regional cloud markets across Asia.

China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology launched the Humanoid Full Lifecycle Management Service Platform, a national initiative to assign every humanoid robot manufactured in China a unique digital identity code. The system will track robots from production through decommissioning. China is the world's largest humanoid robot producer by unit volume, and the digital ID scheme is the first national-level attempt to create a regulatory registry for physical AI systems — a governance model that has no equivalent in the US or Europe yet.

Huawei announced at the 2026 International Symposium on Circuits and Systems in Shanghai that its Mate 90 series, expected this autumn, will debut a new Kirin chip using logic folding technology for the first time. Logic folding moves beyond conventional single-layer chip layouts to stack transistor logic vertically, a technique that could allow Huawei to close the gap with TSMC-manufactured chips despite US export controls. The announcement came from He Tingbo, head of Huawei's semiconductor business, and has received almost no coverage outside Chinese-language tech media.

Malaysia-listed chip design firm Oppstar has refined the structure of a Japan AI chip project and secured a new $2.9 million contract, according to The Edge Malaysia. Oppstar is a small-cap fabless design house that has been quietly building AI chip IP for Japanese customers — a niche that sits entirely outside the NVIDIA-AMD-Intel narrative dominating Western coverage. The contract signals that Japan's domestic AI chip ambitions are generating real commercial flow for Southeast Asian design firms, a supply chain dynamic that has strategic relevance for anyone tracking non-US AI hardware development.

On the research front. Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus has autonomously solved nine open Erdős problems, including two that had resisted mathematicians for 56 years, at a cost of just a few hundred dollars per problem in inference compute. The system uses the Lean compiler to verify every proof step automatically, eliminating the possibility of plausible-sounding but incorrect reasoning. The overall success rate is only about 2.5 percent across attempted problems, but the solved cases include problems that no human team had cracked in over half a century — establishing a new benchmark for AI-assisted formal mathematics.

Researchers from the University of Maryland, Google, and Meta used the AutoTTS framework to demonstrate that a coding agent can autonomously discover compute-scaling algorithms that human researchers would be unlikely to design. The discovered algorithm reduces inference compute by about 70 percent versus standard self-consistency while preserving accuracy. The search cost $40 and completed in 160 minutes. The result matters because it shows that algorithm optimization — previously a months-long research task — can now be delegated to an agent running on commodity inference budget.

The SafeCtrl-RL paper from arxiv introduces an inference-time behavioral control framework that suppresses unsafe outputs in deployed LLMs without any model retraining or parameter modification. A reinforcement learning agent dynamically selects prompt adjustment strategies based on contextual feedback during live dialogue, treating safety as a real-time decision process rather than a training-time constraint. Evaluated across multiple LLMs and unsafe dialogue scenarios, SafeCtrl-RL outperforms existing prompt-based optimization methods — a result that matters for any enterprise deploying customer-facing AI that cannot afford to retrain models on every new safety requirement.

The JT-Safe-V2 paper introduces Safe-MoMA, a framework that orchestrates multiple models and agents to reduce inference costs by more than 30 percent compared to using the largest standalone model, while maintaining comparable performance on both general intelligence and safety benchmarks. The system is designed for enterprise agentic deployments where safety and cost efficiency must be optimized jointly. The 30 percent cost reduction at comparable safety performance is the most concrete infrastructure efficiency result published this week for production agentic systems.
